rationale: The 64-modular order-668 object is the closest known frontier, so the highest-leverage question is whether a local defect CA can outperform non-CA repair under identical coordinates and budgets.
first_step: Reconstruct or recover a canonical 64-modular seed, define one packet basis, and benchmark CA, greedy, tabu, and simulated annealing from the same seed.
expected_signal: A real signal is a strictly higher exact-hit rate or materially faster defect annihilation on solved controls before any order-668 attempt.

rationale: If defect transport is not local enough in matrix coordinates, the next best chance is to make lag residues the state and use message passing only to shape local fields.
first_step: Build a four-channel 167-lag simulator with exact packet deltas and alternate warning-propagation refresh with CA sweeps.
expected_signal: Lower lag-residue entropy and fewer short-cycle failures than either plain warning propagation or plain CA.

rationale: A learned local rule is only valuable if it transfers from solved smaller orders to unseen ones, so transfer should be treated as the first gate rather than as an afterthought.
first_step: Generate corrupted exact matrices from solved small orders and train a compact NCA on one family while holding out others.
expected_signal: Improved exact-repair rate on held-out orders or held-out corruption styles, not just better training reconstruction.

rationale: If local repair methods need better initial states, prime-field CA seed generation is a bounded and testable bridge to cryptographic and MUB-style CA work.
first_step: Enumerate a modest library of F_167 linear or bipermutive rules, project their traces into sign quadruples, and compare the residual distribution against random and m-sequence seeds.
expected_signal: A heavier tail of low-residual seeds that survives a downstream common repair stage.
